## Abstract

This article presents RS-GARCH-LSTM, an extension of the GARCH-LSTM hybrid framework introduced by Zhao et al. (2024) to the cryptocurrency volatility forecasting problem. The key innovation is the replacement of a constant scalar mixing weight with a dynamic gate w_t conditioned on six publicly available Bitcoin on-chain signals, allowing the model to adaptively allocate influence between the GARCH econometric baseline and the LSTM correction component on a daily basis.

The model is evaluated across three experimental settings covering structurally different market conditions: BTC-USD in a normal out-of-sample period, BTC-USD in an unseen stress year (2022, comprising the LUNA and FTX collapses), and ETH-USD in a low-volatility period.

RS-GARCH-LSTM is the only model that passes the Kupiec unconditional coverage test at 99% confidence on BTC in normal conditions (p = 0.063), achieves the highest Kupiec p-value on the unseen 2022 stress scenario (p = 0.501), and delivers a 34.8% reduction in capital efficiency ratio relative to GJR-GARCH on ETH in a period where calibration itself loses discriminating power.

The gate weights, learned end-to-end without prior constraints on sign or magnitude, exhibit direct economic interpretability and are consistent with established on-chain analysis theory.

On a representative \$100M BTC position under Basel III internal model frameworks, the correctly calibrated RS-GARCH-LSTM model releases approximately \$19.2M of excess capital relative to GJR-GARCH, corresponding to an annual opportunity cost of roughly \$960K at a 5% hurdle rate.
